title: Windows CI for the Julia Pkg errors with 'Could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size"'
body: We have a failing Julia package build with DuckDB_jll 1.1.0 on Windows GitHub runners. Precompilation fails with `could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size": The specified procedure could not be found.` I created a minimal reproducer: Ubuntu passes with DuckDB_jll 1.0.0 and 1.1.0, Windows passes with 1.0.0, and Windows fails with 1.1.0. The package code does not run because the failure occurs during precompilation.

symptoms_visible: On Windows, Julia package precompilation with DuckDB_jll 1.1.0 stops with `could not load symbol "duckdb_vector_size": The specified procedure could not be found`; the same reproducer passes on Ubuntu and with DuckDB_jll 1.0.0 on Windows.
N0.label: N0 Windows Julia precompilation failure reported

symptoms_visible: The same missing-symbol precompilation error occurs on local Windows machines and on several Windows 10 computers, including with DuckDB.jl 1.1.0.
N1.label: N1 Windows scope and matching Julia version confirmed

symptoms_visible: After updating DuckDB_jll to 1.1.2, Julia still stops during precompilation with the same missing `duckdb_vector_size` error.
N1_x.label: N1_x JLL version-bump aftermath

symptoms_visible: The BinaryBuilder-produced DuckDB_jll DLL gives the missing-symbol error, while Julia precompiles successfully when `JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY` points to the official Windows `duckdb.dll`.
Pinning DuckDB_jll to 1.0.0 also lets the package precompile.
N2.label: N2 failure isolated to the BinaryBuilder Windows DLL

symptoms_visible: The generated Windows DLL still cannot provide `duckdb_vector_size` to Julia, even though that symbol is present in the C-API object file and intermediate object archive.
N3.label: N3 final-link export loss demonstrated

symptoms_visible: With a Windows DuckDB library containing the export fix, Julia finds `duckdb_vector_size` and DuckDB.jl precompiles successfully.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does this only fail in GitHub Actions, or can you reproduce it on a local Windows machine?
Can anyone reproduce the same precompilation error on another Windows computer?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is broken on our local Windows machines too, not just CI. I can also reproduce the same error on several Windows 10 computers and on a fresh Julia installation.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only fails in one GitHub Actions job; the same versions precompile correctly on every local Windows machine we tested.
It reproduces on Windows 11 machines rather than Windows 10, with the same missing symbol.

question_patterns: Does it still fail when DuckDB.jl and DuckDB_jll are both on the 1.1 line?
Was this only a DuckDB.jl 1.0 and DuckDB_jll 1.1 mismatch?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Originally DuckDB.jl 1.1.0 was not available, but I reran the reproducer after it was released. DuckDB.jl 1.1.0 still fails on Windows with the same `duckdb_vector_size` error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Matching DuckDB.jl 1.1.0 with DuckDB_jll 1.1.0 works; the error only occurs when DuckDB.jl 1.0 is combined with the newer JLL.

edges.comment: The local-machine and additional Windows confirmations came from several affected participants; they are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Resolve the failure by rebuilding and updating DuckDB_jll to a newer upstream DuckDB release without changing the Windows build/export configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Update the Yggdrasil recipe and install DuckDB_jll 1.1.2, assuming the newer upstream binary version contains the needed fix.

edges.comment: A JLL rebuild/update to 1.1.2 was actually produced and installed, but the same precompilation error remained. A version bump without correcting the Windows export behavior is therefore falsified.

question_patterns: Can you test the official Windows DuckDB DLL by setting `JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY` to its path?
Does Julia precompile if you point it at the DuckDB-provided `duckdb.dll` instead of the JLL library?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I downloaded the official Windows C/C++ library, set `JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY` to its `duckdb.dll`, and the latest DuckDB.jl precompiled successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The official Windows DLL gives exactly the same missing `duckdb_vector_size` error.
The official DLL works when selected through an absolute path rather than a relative path.

question_patterns: Does the result differ between the official DuckDB DLL and the BinaryBuilder/Yggdrasil DLL at the same version?
Is this specific to the library packaged by DuckDB_jll?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The official 1.1.2 Windows library works, but the 1.1.2 library built through Yggdrasil and installed by DuckDB_jll still gives the precompilation error. I attached the Windows build-requirements screenshot I was comparing against.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both DLLs work at 1.1.2, so there is no difference between the official and BinaryBuilder artifacts.

question_patterns: Does pinning DuckDB_jll to the last working version let users precompile in the meantime?
Can you confirm whether DuckDB_jll 1.0.0 is a viable temporary workaround?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. `add DuckDB_jll@v1.0.0` followed by `pin DuckDB_jll@v1.0.0` avoids the error. Pinning DuckDB itself to v0.10.3 is another temporary option.

question_patterns: What Windows build requirements were you using for comparison?
Can you share the relevant Windows build documentation you checked?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I compared the Yggdrasil build with DuckDB's documented Windows build requirements and attached the relevant screenshot.

edges.comment: These tests were performed by multiple affected users and contributors and are folded into one user side. The official-DLL and pinned-version checks are measurements of alternative binaries; neither is the permanent source fix.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the export table of the failing DLL and check whether the DuckDB C API symbols are present?
What symbols does the BinaryBuilder-produced Windows DLL actually export?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I inspected the failing Windows DLL. I cannot find the DuckDB C-API exports such as `duckdb_vector_size`, while the ADBC symbols are present.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing DLL export table contains `duckdb_vector_size` with the expected undecorated name.
Several other DuckDB C-API symbols are missing along with `duckdb_vector_size`; the ADBC exports remain present.

question_patterns: Can you bisect the source revisions using the MinGW Windows build to identify the first bad commit?
What raw result do you get from a good/bad commit bisection?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced the problem outside BinaryBuilder and bisected it. The first build that gives me the bad DLL is commit `d1ea1538c9217fb536485f1500f04a0b55b1e584`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same source commit produces a working DLL outside BinaryBuilder, and the bisection points only to a BinaryBuilder toolchain update.

question_patterns: Can you trace `duckdb_vector_size` through the object file, intermediate archive, and final DLL?
At which build artifact does the C-API symbol disappear?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Using `nm`, I see `duckdb_vector_size` in `ub_duckdb_main_capi.cpp.obj` and in `CMakeFiles/duckdb.dir/objects.a`. When I inspect the final `libduckdb.dll`, the C-API export is no longer there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The symbol is already absent from the compiled C-API object file, before the archive and DLL link steps.
The same symbol is present at a different address in the object and archive, but is still absent from the final DLL.

question_patterns: Was `-fvisibility=hidden` newly introduced in the failing JLL build?
Do older working DuckDB_jll Windows build logs contain the same visibility flag?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I downloaded logs from older working DuckDB_jll Windows releases, including 1.0.0+3. Those builds also contain `-fvisibility=hidden`, so the flag was already present when the DLL worked.

edges.comment: Technical investigation from contributing users is merged into the simulated user side. The answers contain raw bisection and binary-inspection output; concluding that the final MinGW shared-library link mishandles C-API exports is engineer-side inference.

solution.intent: Fix the MinGW Windows shared-library export path so the final BinaryBuilder/Yggdrasil DLL retains the DuckDB C-API exports, apply DuckDB PR #16397, and have the reporter verify a Windows build containing that fix.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the Windows export/linking correction from DuckDB PR #16397 so C-API functions such as `duckdb_vector_size` are exported by the final MinGW-built `libduckdb.dll`; rebuild DuckDB_jll from that source and ask the user to retest precompilation on Windows. The change is scheduled to land in DuckDB v1.2.1.
solution.inference_hint: The user-side evidence establishes that the symbol exists in the compiled object and archive but is absent from the final MinGW-built DLL, while an official same-version DLL works. Interpreting this as a Windows shared-link/export handling defect and mapping it to the correction in PR #16397 is the engineering conclusion, not a conclusion that should be placed in the user's raw measurement answers.

edges.comment: Maintainer resolution: PR #16397 fixes the problem and is planned for v1.2.1. The graph requires a user retest of a build containing the landed change before the issue is treated as observably resolved.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as the MinGW/BinaryBuilder Windows shared-library build failing to retain or expose DuckDB C-API symbols in the final DLL, even though those symbols exist in the compiled object and intermediate archive.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the binary comparison and inspection evidence: the official Windows DLL works, the JLL DLL lacks C-API exports while retaining ADBC exports, and `duckdb_vector_size` disappears only by the final DLL stage.

Must propose the permanent upstream DuckDB Windows export/linking correction that restores the C-API exports, followed by rebuilding the JLL; pinning DuckDB_jll 1.0.0 or setting `JULIA_DUCKDB_LIBRARY` may be offered only as temporary workarounds.
Must not claim that updating DuckDB_jll to 1.1.2 alone fixes the issue, because that update was tested and produced the same precompilation error.
Must not settle on removing `-fvisibility=hidden` solely because it appears in the failing command: older working JLL Windows builds used the same flag.
Must ask the reporter to verify Julia precompilation on Windows using a build that contains the export fix before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: The opening reporter is a technically capable Julia package maintainer who can create minimal CI reproducers, manage package compatibility bounds, and test package versions. Other folded-in contributors are able to inspect DLL exports, cross-compile with MinGW, trace linker artifacts, and bisect source commits.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-driven. Provides exact version matrices, CI links, commands, and raw binary-inspection output; clearly separates temporary user workarounds from work intended to repair the packaged binary.
